lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In July nineteen sixty-nine, a ship found a racing yacht drifting in the middle of the Atlantic.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: It was the Tin-muth Electron, sailed alone by Donald Crowhurst in a race around the world.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: For months, his radio reports had put him far ahead.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But his logbooks were still on board.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: For seven months, he wandered the South Atlantic and radioed fake positions.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: He even stopped secretly in Argentina, which broke the rules.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then his final pages turned into twenty-five thousand words of strange philosophy.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The last entry, on July first, ended with four words.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The chronometer case was found empty.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: So what happened on that empty deck?
